claim.quote: Here the T2K collaboration reports a measurement that favors large enhancement of the neutrino oscillation probability, excluding values of dCP which result in a large enhancement of the observed anti-neutrino oscillation probability at three standard deviations (3 sigma). ... Our results show an indication of CP violation in the lepton sector.

date.note: A16: the result was first made public via the arXiv v1 submission (9 October 2019), earlier than the Nature publication (2020); the earlier date is used per A16/A9. Published as Nature 580, 339-344 (2020).

key_value_text.note: The intervals are quoted verbatim; which CP-conserving values they exclude follows from them (−π ≡ π lies inside the normal-ordering interval). Corrected 2026-10-25: an earlier wording said both 0 and ±π were excluded at 3σ, which the cited abstract does not support.
key_value_text.quote: The 3 sigma confidence level interval for dCP, which is cyclic and repeats every 2pi, is [-3.41,-0.03] for the so-called normal mass ordering, and [-2.54,-0.32] for the inverted mass ordering.
key_value_text.value: δCP 3σ confidence interval [−3.41, −0.03] (normal mass ordering) or [−2.54, −0.32] (inverted mass ordering): δCP = 0 lies outside both intervals; π is outside the inverted-ordering interval but inside the normal-ordering one (−π ≈ −3.14)

name: T2K constraint on the CP-violating phase in neutrino oscillations

significance.note: 'δCP = 0 excluded' follows from the quoted 3σ intervals (0 lies outside both); 'not a discovery' restates the collaboration's wording 'an indication'.
significance.quote: excluding values of dCP which result in a large enhancement of the observed anti-neutrino oscillation probability at three standard deviations (3 sigma) ... Our results show an indication of CP violation in the lepton sector.
significance.value: 3σ (δCP = 0 excluded; an indication of CP violation, not a discovery)

summary.plain: T2K compared how often neutrinos and antineutrinos change type on their way across Japan and found a difference that excludes, at 3-sigma confidence, the CP-conserving value δCP = 0. The collaboration words it carefully as 'an indication of CP violation' — not yet a discovery.
summary.technical: Combined neutrino- and antineutrino-mode appearance and disappearance data give 3σ intervals for δCP of [−3.41, −0.03] (normal ordering) and [−2.54, −0.32] (inverted ordering): δCP = 0 is excluded at 3σ in both orderings, π only for the inverted ordering. The collaboration reports 'an indication of CP violation in the lepton sector'.

title: Constraint on the Matter-Antimatter Symmetry-Violating Phase in Neutrino Oscillations
why_it_matters: It excludes the CP-conserving value δCP = 0 at 3σ — an indication that neutrinos and antineutrinos oscillate differently (CP violation in the lepton sector), a possible ingredient of the matter-antimatter asymmetry of the universe through leptogenesis. The paper closes by saying that future measurements with larger data samples will determine whether the leptonic CP violation is larger than the quark-sector CP violation.
